title: Re-work commit-message editing to route edits into the implementable review
description:
The UI commit-message editor works and captures edits in the right shape, but the edits are POSTed to /api/record-feedback (the pattern-analysis snapshot in ~/.umpire/feedback/) instead of /api/review (the per-review deliverable in .umpire/reviews/ that an agent implements). Result, editing a commit message never affects the commit, because nothing acts on an individual snapshot.

Rework decisions (confirmed with user). Route commit-message edits into the review output ONLY (.umpire/reviews/review-*.json) and stop writing them to the analysis snapshot. Represent them as a dedicated structured field (commit_message_edits array) on the review. Keep editing BOTH subject (title) and body, so the implementing agent rewrites the full message.

An agent reading the review JSON then rewrites the commit message as part of implementing the feedback. The existing frontend collectCommitMessageEdits() already emits sha plus original_subject, original_body, edited_subject, edited_body, with original included for agent context.
close_reason: Epic complete. Commit-message edits now route into the implementable review deliverable (.umpire/reviews/) as a dedicated commit_message_edits field carrying both subject and body, and no longer into the pattern-analysis snapshot. Delivered across umpire-2le (model and handler), umpire-g7k (frontend submit plus relaxed guard), umpire-wq6 (snapshot removal), and umpire-14p (review checkpoint). Commits 0bf33f9, d359720, a018e5b, 3939536.

title: Review handoff depends on dismissing the feedback prompt, which users have no reason to do
description:
The /umpire skill relies on umpire's process exit as the signal that a review is ready, because that is the only event the harness can wake an agent on. But the frontend does not shut down at submit: app.js replaces the submit bar with "Record this feedback to improve future Claude sessions?" and only calls /api/shutdown when Yes or No is clicked.

A user who submits their review and stops there -- which is the natural thing to do, the review is submitted -- leaves the server running forever. The agent waits on a process exit that never comes, and from the user's side Claude simply never picks the review up.

Confirmed in a live test: review-20260916-073936.json was saved, ~/.umpire/feedback/ was empty, and the umpire process was still alive afterwards.

The plan chose exit over submission deliberately, reasoning it was the more accurate signal. It is more accurate and less reliable, and reliability matters more here.

Options: fold the feedback question into the submit form so one action submits and exits, or shut down on submit and drop the post-submit prompt, or keep the current flow and have the skill warn the user about the second step.

Found by the live session test in umpire-acp.7.
close_reason: Not a bug -- Zach confirmed the current shutdown behavior is intended. The feedback prompt stays as the thing that closes the server. What was missing was telling the user, so SKILL.md now says at launch that submitting isn't the last step and that answering the feedback question is what hands the session back, and the pickup section no longer implies exit follows submission directly. Commit 5114a29.

title: Sign and notarize the macOS binaries with an Apple Developer ID
description: Signing and notarizing the macOS binaries with an Apple Developer ID is the clean, long-term fix for the Gatekeeper 'could not verify free of malware' warning, replacing the postflight xattr quarantine-strip stopgap shipped in v0.8.1 (umpire-4do). This is optional best-practice, NOT deadline-driven. umpire ships through the third-party tap z-morgan/homebrew-tap, which is not subject to Homebrew's official-tap Gatekeeper audit or its 2026-09-01 disabling of unsigned casks. That deadline applies only to the main Homebrew/cask repo. Motivation for doing this anyway: notarized binaries pass Gatekeeper even when quarantined, so we stop leaning on a bypass that Apple could disable in a future macOS, and the install UX stays clean. Requires Apple Developer Program membership (about 99 USD per year) and a Developer ID Application certificate. Wire signing and notarization into the release pipeline via GoReleaser notarize/sign, anchore/quill, or xcrun notarytool run on a macOS CI runner.

title: Teach the skill to pick up and act on a submitted review
description:
Extend skills/umpire/SKILL.md with what happens after the process exits.

Finding the review: read the background task output and look for the printed path. Fall back to the newest file in .umpire/reviews/ if it is not there.

Interpreting it: the anchoring contract currently lives only in Go doc comments on review.Comment, where an agent reading the JSON will never see it. Restate it in the skill.

  - commit_sha empty means the comment was authored against the full base..head diff, so line_start refers to the head revision and can be trusted directly.
  - commit_sha set means line_start is relative to that commit's diff, and diff_hunk is the authoritative locator, because a later commit may have shifted the same line in the head revision.

Commit message edits carry their own instruction field, and the body hard-wraps at 72 columns.

Acting on it:

  1. If the review contains questions, answer them and stop. No code changes until the user has replied. Review comments are not uniformly change orders — an agent that reads "why did you do it this way?" as an instruction produces a confident non-answer and edits code that did not need editing.
  2. Otherwise implement the feedback by amending the commits the comments landed on, not by appending fixups to the tip. Every comment already knows its commit. Non-interactively, that is git commit --fixup=<sha> followed by GIT_SEQUENCE_EDITOR=true git rebase --autosquash <merge-base>.
  3. Comments with no commit_sha have no single commit to amend. Those become a new commit at the tip.

title: Guard the branch rewrite and the sandbox failure modes
description:
Step 4 hands an agent the ability to rewrite a branch from a JSON file. This is the seatbelt.

The one that matters: check whether the branch has already been pushed before rewriting it. A successful git rev-parse @{upstream} means a rebase rewrites published history, which is the user's call and not the agent's. Stop and ask.

Also cover:

  - The cancel path. The user changes their mind and never submits, so the background process would otherwise hang forever. Kill the task.
  - Base and head resolving to the same commit. Say so rather than opening an empty review UI.
  - Sandbox troubleshooting. Claude Code's Bash sandbox blocks both things umpire needs, verified on 2.1.273: binding a listener on 127.0.0.1 fails with EPERM, and writing to ~/.umpire/feedback/ fails the same way. The fix is settings rather than disabling the sandbox wholesale — sandbox.network.allowLocalBinding true, and ~/.umpire on the sandbox.filesystem.write allowlist. Browser auto-open may additionally need Mach lookup since open goes through LaunchServices. Unverified, and it only degrades to the user clicking the printed URL.

title: Report when the browser fails to open instead of discarding the error
description:
runReview calls browser.Open(url) and throws the error away, and browser.Open uses cmd.Start() so it wouldn't catch a non-zero exit anyway. Under a Bash sandbox, 'open <url>' fails with LaunchServices -600 procNotFound at _LSAnnotateAndSendAppleEventWithOptions: the browser app is activated but the Apple Event carrying the URL is refused, so the browser comes to the front with no new tab.

Umpire says nothing, so the user sees their browser focus and assume it worked, and an agent driving umpire via /umpire confidently reports that the review is open in the browser.

Switch browser.Open to Run() so the exit status is visible, surface the helper's stderr, and have runReview print a fallback line pointing at the already-printed URL.

Found by the live /umpire session test in umpire-acp.7.
close_reason: browser.Open now uses Run() instead of Start() so the helper's exit status is visible, and carries its stderr on the returned error. runReview prints a fallback line pointing at the already-printed URL. Root cause confirmed by reproducing it: LaunchServices -600 procNotFound from _LSAnnotateAndSendAppleEventWithOptions -- the browser app gets activated (the focus change the user saw) but the Apple Event carrying the URL is refused (the missing tab). The two sandbox keys do NOT fix this, so SKILL.md and the README both stopped implying otherwise, and the skill now tells the agent not to claim the browser opened. Tested with a stub 'open' on PATH. Commit c20f007.

title: Add a CI workflow running build/test/vet on push and pull_request
description:
Today .github/workflows/ has only release.yml (triggered on v* tags). Nothing runs on push or pull_request. Deferred because no outside contributors are expected yet, so per-PR checks would only gate commits by Zach. Accepted consequence -- nothing automatically prevents a regression of the SEC-1 loopback bind or the SEC-2 host/origin middleware. Their regression tests exist but must be run locally (go test ./...) rather than enforced by a check.

When implemented: a workflow on push/pull_request running go build ./..., go test ./..., go vet ./..., and gofmt -l. Four notes. (1) gofmt -l lists offending files but exits 0, so a naive step never fails -- assert on empty output (or use -exec false), or the lint step is decoration. (2) Pin setup-go with go-version-file: go.mod so CI tracks the toolchain floor rather than drifting from it. (3) Skip golangci-lint initially -- its default linters will flag existing code, meaning a cleanup pass or a suppression config. Add it deliberately when someone will fix what it finds. (4) CI only works if the check is required by branch protection -- advisory-only CI gets ignored once it goes red, which is a GitHub settings change, not code.

Reference: audit doc Part 2, Bead B (PROD-1). Revisit when people other than Zach start opening PRs.

title: Commit-level comments in the commit pane
description:
Let a reviewer leave a note about a whole commit, not just a line. A textarea renders in the commit pane (`#commit-header`) underneath the commit message card, and the note rides along in the saved review JSON as a new `commit_comments` array.

## Design decisions settled during planning

**Placement** — sibling appended to `#commit-header` AFTER the `.commit-message` element, not nested inside it. `startEditingCommitMessage()` (web/static/js/app.js:353) replaces the whole `.commit-message` node with an editor, so a nested textarea would be destroyed and rebuilt empty every time Edit is clicked.

**Persistence** — live write to `App.commitComments` on the textarea's `input` event. No Save/Cancel buttons: a comment has no original to revert to, unlike a commit-message edit. Because state is captured on every keystroke, the box needs no entry in `flushPendingEdits()`.

**Data shape** — a new `CommitComment{SHA, Subject, Body}` type in the review package, carried on `Review.CommitComments` and `SubmitRequest.CommitComments`. Do NOT reuse the existing `Comment` type with an empty file/line_start. That would break the anchoring contract documented at internal/review/review.go:36-46.

**Feedback snapshots** — commit comments stay out of `~/.umpire/feedback/`. Commit a018e5b deliberately removed commit-message edits from the snapshot because carrying them in two places duplicated data and implied the snapshot acted on them. The same reasoning applies here.

## Commit order

The Go type lands before the frontend sends the field. Go's JSON decoder silently drops unknown fields, so wiring the frontend first would fail quietly rather than loudly. This mirrors how the commit-message-edit feature was sequenced (0bf33f9 then d359720).

## Out of scope

Sidebar badges marking commented commits, threading or replies, comments on the "All changes" view (no `#commit-header` exists there), feedback snapshots.
close_reason: All four children landed: comment box in the commit pane (7c940fe), CommitComment on Review/SubmitRequest (e7fee65), submission wiring (6e168d7 plus 1275819 threading the field through API.submitReview), and the footer count (4f3c0fb). Verified end to end by running umpire against HEAD~4..main: typed a note, navigated away and back, opened the message editor without losing it, and submitted a review whose only content was the note, which saved with a populated commit_comments array. All four design decisions recorded here were followed as written. Sidebar badges, threading, All-changes comments, and feedback snapshots remain out of scope.

title: Render a comment box under the commit message in the commit pane

In web/static/css/app.css: styles for the new block, modeled on `.commit-message-body-input` (app.css:309). Use `box-sizing: border-box` and `width: 100%` so the box respects the pane width that `sizeCommitHeader()` computes from a 72-column reference.

title: Count commit comments in the review total

title: Teach Claude: accumulate review feedback for config training

On the 5th opt-in and beyond, offer a generated prompt the user can paste into a Claude Code session to analyze patterns and propose updates to user-level config (~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, ~/.claude/settings.json). See docs/plans/20260421-teach-claude.md for full design.

title: Add internal/feedback package — data model and storage
description:
Create internal/feedback/ package with three files:

**snapshot.go**: Snapshot struct and SubmitRequest struct.
- Snapshot fields: Version (int), CreatedAt (time.Time), RepoPath (string), BaseRef, HeadRef, BaseSHA, HeadSHA (strings), Diff (string), Review (embedded struct with Summary string + Comments []review.Comment).
- SubmitRequest fields: Diff (string), Review (same embedded struct) — this is the JSON body the frontend POSTs.

**store.go**: Store struct with Dir field (string, defaults to ~/.umpire/feedback/).
- Save(s *Snapshot) (string, error): MkdirAll the Dir, set CreatedAt/Version, marshal to JSON, write to snapshot-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.json. Return path.
- Count() (int, error): Glob for snapshot-*.json files in Dir, return count.

**prompt.go**: GeneratePrompt(count int) string: Build a self-contained prompt string for the user to paste into Claude Code. The prompt instructs Claude to:
1. Read all JSON files in ~/.umpire/feedback/
2. For each snapshot, understand the diff and review comments
3. Classify feedback as generalizable preferences vs one-off corrections — only patterns produce config changes
4. Look for recurring themes: naming conventions, error handling style, architectural preferences, testing expectations
5. Read existing user-level config: ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md and ~/.claude/settings.json
6. Propose additions/edits without duplicating or contradicting existing rules — user-level config only
7. Present proposed changes for approval before applying
8. After changes applied, delete processed snapshot files from ~/.umpire/feedback/
The prompt should embed the count so Claude knows how many snapshots to expect.

**Tests**: store_test.go covering Save (writes valid JSON, sets version/timestamp) and Count (returns correct count including zero case).
close_reason: Implemented snapshot.go, store.go, prompt.go, and store_test.go. All tests pass.

title: Add post-submission feedback flow in frontend
description:
Modify the frontend to handle the post-submission feedback recording flow.

**Changes to web/static/js/app.js — submitReview():**

After the review is saved, instead of showing 'Server shutting down...' immediately, render a multi-step inline flow in the submit bar:

Step 1: Show success + question:
  'Review saved to <path>'
  'Record this feedback to improve future Claude sessions?  [Yes] [No thanks]'

Step 2a — No thanks: POST /api/shutdown, show 'Server shutting down...'

Step 2b — Yes (threshold not reached): POST /api/record-feedback with {diff: App.fullDiff, review: {summary, comments}}. Show 'Feedback recorded (N of 5 until analysis is available). Server shutting down...' Then POST /api/shutdown.

Step 2c — Yes (threshold reached): Same POST, then show 'Feedback recorded — N snapshots available. Generate a prompt to analyze your feedback and propose Claude config updates? [Copy Prompt to Clipboard] [Not now]'
  - Copy Prompt: GET /api/feedback-prompt, copy prompt text to clipboard via navigator.clipboard.writeText(), then POST /api/shutdown
  - Not now: POST /api/shutdown

**Cache the full diff:**
In loadFullDiff(), after fetching the diff, store it as this.fullDiff = diff. This makes the base..head diff available at submission time for the feedback snapshot.

**New API methods in web/static/js/api.js:**
- recordFeedback({diff, review}): POST /api/record-feedback, return JSON
- getFeedbackPrompt(): GET /api/feedback-prompt, return JSON
- shutdown(): POST /api/shutdown

**CSS in web/static/css/app.css:**
Style the feedback question and buttons to match the existing submit bar aesthetic. The buttons should use existing .btn, .btn-submit, and .btn-cancel classes. Add a .feedback-message class for the status text with color: var(--text-secondary) and margin-top: 0.25rem.

title: Add API endpoints and wire feedback store into server
description:
Add feedback-related API endpoints and restructure the shutdown flow.

**New endpoints in internal/server/handlers.go:**

POST /api/record-feedback: Accept SubmitRequest JSON body ({diff, review}). Build a feedback.Snapshot from the request body + ReviewContext metadata (repo path from Repo.Dir, refs, SHAs). Save via feedback.Store. Return JSON {count: N, threshold_reached: bool} where threshold is count >= 5.

GET /api/feedback-prompt: Call feedback.GeneratePrompt(store.Count()) and return JSON {prompt: string}.

POST /api/shutdown: Send to the shutdown channel. Return 200. This replaces the auto-shutdown-on-review-submit behavior.

**Changes to ReviewContext (handlers.go):**
- Add FeedbackStore *feedback.Store field
- Add ShutdownFn func() field (called by /api/shutdown handler)
- Remove OnSubmit callback — review submission no longer triggers shutdown

**Changes to cmd/root.go:**
- Resolve ~/.umpire/feedback/ path and create feedback.Store
- Pass FeedbackStore into ReviewContext
- Set ShutdownFn to send on submitCh
- Remove the OnSubmit callback from ReviewContext (POST /api/review no longer triggers shutdown)
- The select loop stays the same — it still waits on submitCh, but now /api/shutdown is what sends to it instead of handleReview

**Changes to POST /api/review (handleReview):**
- Remove the go rc.OnSubmit(...) call at the end
- The handler just saves the review and returns the path — shutdown is now driven by the frontend via /api/shutdown

description: The v0.8.1 Release run logged a GitHub annotation that actions/checkout@v4, actions/setup-go@v5, and goreleaser/goreleaser-action@v6 target Node.js 20, which is deprecated and is being force-run on Node 24. title: Embed a body line-wrapping instruction in the saved review JSON for edited commit messages
description:
Problem: When a reviewer rewrites a commit message during review, the edits are captured as commit_message_edits and saved to the review JSON (internal/review/review.go CommitMessageEdit, assembled in internal/server/handlers.go handleReview near line 96, written by internal/review/store.go to .umpire/reviews/review-TIMESTAMP.json). Nothing in the saved file tells the applying agent to re-wrap the body, so an agent applying an edit could write a long, unwrapped body.

Goal: Embed an agent-facing instruction in the review JSON, populated only when commit message edits are present, telling the agent to apply standard git commit-message line-wrapping (hard-wrap the body at 72 columns) to any commit message it edits.

Scope note (from Zach): instruct ONLY the body line-wrapping and line-length rule. Do NOT mention subject length.

Recommended approach: add a field to the Review struct, for example CommitMessageEditInstructions string with json tag commit_message_edit_instructions,omitempty, and set it in handleReview only when len(req.CommitMessageEdits) is greater than 0. Wording is at the implementer's discretion -- keep it concise, along the lines of: When applying these commit message edits, hard-wrap the body at 72 columns, per standard git commit conventions. Because CommitMessageEdits already uses omitempty, the review JSON stays clean for reviews that make no message edits.

Also tighten the CommitMessageEdit doc comment (internal/review/review.go near lines 18-27) to reference the same 72-column rule, so the documented contract and the emitted file agree. Optional but recommended.

Files: internal/review/review.go (Review struct plus the CommitMessageEdit doc comment), internal/server/handlers.go (handleReview near line 96). Tests: internal/server/handlers_test.go and/or internal/review/store_test.go -- add a case asserting the instruction is present when edits exist and omitted when they do not.

Verify: submit a review with a commit-message edit and confirm the saved review-TIMESTAMP.json includes the instruction field. Submit one without edits and confirm the field is omitted.
close_reason: Added review.CommitMessageEditWrapInstruction and a Review.CommitMessageEditInstructions field (json commit_message_edit_instructions,omitempty). handleReview populates it only when req.CommitMessageEdits is non-empty, so reviews without message edits stay clean. Tightened the CommitMessageEdit doc comment to name the same 72-column body rule. Tests assert the instruction is present with edits and the key is omitted without. gofmt/vet/test all green. Committed in 5a06b7b.

title: Copy button next to the saved review path after submit
description: After a review is submitted, the saved review JSON path is shown in the submit bar. Add a copy button next to that filename so the user can copy the path to the clipboard (mirroring the existing feedback-prompt copy affordance).
close_reason: Added a Copy button beside the saved review path in the submit bar, wired attachSavedPathCopy across all post-submit states. Committed in 96614c5.

title: Restore the "Files changed" sidebar tab with working file navigation and rename support
description:
The "Files changed" sidebar tab was hidden (its button removed from sidebar.js init) to eliminate a broken interaction (BUG-1). renderFiles, scrollToFile, API.getFiles, and the /api/files endpoint remain in place but unreachable, so restoring the tab is close to a one-line revert. This bead covers restoring it correctly AND fixing the rename parsing bug (BUG-2) that the tab depends on. File one bead for both because they are coupled -- the BUG-2 parser fix depends on a rendering contract that only exists once the tab is back.

BUG-1 (file-switcher does nothing in per-commit view): The tab is populated from GET /api/files (every file changed across base..head), but the rendered diff on load (and when a single commit is selected) contains only one commit files. Clicking a file from a different commit finds no matching DOM node, so scrollToFile silently does nothing. Agreed fix (decided 2026-08-12) -- clicking a file should ALWAYS put the user in the full-range view. On click: (1) if not already showing the full diff, call App.loadFullDiff() and clear Sidebar.activeCommitSHA. (2) WAIT for the re-render to complete, THEN scrollToFile(path). loadFullDiff fetches /api/diff and re-renders via diff2html, so calling scrollToFile synchronously after it searches a stale DOM and reproduces the no-op. Chain off the render, do NOT fire-and-forget (most likely step to get wrong). (3) if already in full-diff view, skip the reload and just scroll. Also make scrollToFile console.warn on a miss instead of being a silent no-op. Add regression coverage for clicking a file that lives in a non-active commit.

BUG-2 (renamed files mishandled by --name-status parsing) in internal/git/git.go ChangedFiles(): git diff --name-status emits THREE tab-separated fields for a rename or copy -- Rxxx TAB old TAB new. SplitN(line, TAB, 2) collapses this into Status=Rxxx and Path=(old TAB new). Impact once the tab is back: statusLabels lookup misses (shows raw R100), and Path contains an embedded tab plus both paths so it never matches diff2html .d2h-file-name. Fix: split into up to three fields, strip the similarity score from R/C statuses, use the NEW path as Path (optionally keep old path for display), add a unit test with a rename fixture. Confirm the chosen Path matches what diff2html renders as the file name (it renders a rename header roughly as old-arrow-new), which is why this waits for the tab. Latent today -- /api/files is unreachable, and the only other caller (cmd/root.go changed-files count) reads only len(files), which stays correct.

Reference: audit doc Part 2, Bead A.

title: Click collapsed-lines row in diff to expand context
description: In the diff view, the blue rows representing collapsed/hidden lines should be clickable. Clicking should expand the collapsed lines, matching GitHub's behavior (expand by the same default number of lines GitHub uses).
close_reason: Diff expander now computes the original gap once at attach time and stores it on the info row's dataset. Subsequent clicks read the remaining gap and fetch the next 20-line batch from the bottom up, correctly walking through multi-batch gaps. Previously the second click was re-reading the just-inserted lines as the gap boundary and dropping the unfetched upper portion.

title: Remove commit-message edits from the analysis snapshot path
description:
Now that edits flow through the review, take them out of the pattern-analysis snapshot per the review-output-only decision.

In internal/feedback/snapshot.go, remove the CommitMessageEdit type and the CommitMessageEdits field from Snapshot and SubmitRequest. In internal/server/handlers.go handleRecordFeedback, drop the CommitMessageEdits assignment. In web/static/js/app.js recordFeedback(), drop commit_message_edits from the payload, and in web/static/js/api.js drop the param from recordFeedback().

Tests. Move the existing commit-edit assertion out of the record-feedback handler test (internal/server/handlers_test.go) and trim internal/feedback/store_test.go so it no longer asserts commit edits. The snapshot keeps capturing summary, comments, and diff for pattern learning.

Depends on the frontend sending edits via /api/review first (umpire-g7k). See epic umpire-1b6.
close_reason: Removed CommitMessageEdit type and commit_message_edits field from Snapshot and SubmitRequest in feedback/snapshot.go, dropped the assignment in handleRecordFeedback, and stopped recordFeedback()/api.js from sending the field. Converted the record-feedback handler test to assert snapshot persistence of summary+diff, and trimmed feedback/store_test.go. CommitMessageEdit now lives only in the review package. Build and tests green. Committed in a018e5b.

title: Auto-save pending edits when navigating between commits
description: When the user navigates commits via the arrow buttons or by clicking a commit in the side-nav, any unsaved changes (commit message subject/body, and open line-comment forms) should be persisted automatically, exactly as if Save were clicked. Only an explicit Cancel discards a change.
close_reason: Navigation now flushes in-progress edits via App.flushPendingEdits(), called from navigateCommit (arrow buttons/keys) and the sidebar commit-item click. persistCommitMessageEdit extracted so the commit-message editor saves without the empty-subject alert. Open comment forms are flushed by clicking their Save buttons. Committed in 8bcf187.

title: Add resizable panes via drag handle
description: Add a drag handle between the sidebar and diff container panes so users can resize them by hovering the edge (seeing cursor change to col-resize), clicking, and dragging. Implement via a resize handle div, CSS for cursor/styling, and JS for mousedown/mousemove/mouseup drag logic.
close_reason: Added resize handle div between sidebar and diff-container with mousedown/mousemove/mouseup drag logic, col-resize cursor, and blue highlight on hover/drag

title: Auto-size the commit-message pane to a standard git commit-message width
description:
Problem: When traversing commits, the commit-message pane (#commit-header, web/static/css/app.css:200) has a fixed default width of 25vw. A commit body is hard-wrapped at ~72 columns with real newlines and is rendered in .commit-message-body -- a pre element with white-space pre-wrap and font-family inherit (a proportional font) at app.css:339. Because the pane is usually narrower than a 72-column line, each hard-wrapped source line ALSO soft-wraps inside the pane, producing a ragged double-wrapped look.

Goal: Default the pane width so a standard-formatted commit body (72-column hard wrap) fits without soft-wrapping, and keep that width consistent as the user navigates between commits. Preserve the existing drag-to-resize (Resize.attachCommitHeaderDrag in web/static/js/resize.js) as the user override, so the user can adjust the width from there.

Recommended approach (CSS-first): render .commit-message-body in a monospace font and cap its wrap width at 72 columns (width 72ch), then let #commit-header hug that width (width fit-content or max-content) with a viewport-capped max-width and the existing min-width. A monospace 72ch is an exact, font-relative measure, so the pane chrome (pane padding 0.75rem 1rem, plus the .commit-message padding and border) falls out naturally. Switch the edit textarea .commit-message-body-input (app.css:309) to monospace too, so editing matches the rendered width.

Alternative if fit-content fights the sticky or flex layout: measure a 72-char monospace string in JS inside renderCommitHeader (web/static/js/app.js:152) and set header.style.width, clamped to the Resize MIN/MAX bounds. That matches the existing JS-driven sizing style.

Note: the pane is torn down and rebuilt on every commit navigation (removeCommitHeader then renderCommitHeader), so a manual drag width already resets when moving between commits. This change does not regress that. If width persistence across navigation is wanted, file a separate follow-up.

Files: web/static/css/app.css (#commit-header near line 200, .commit-message-body near 339, .commit-message-body-input near 309). Possibly web/static/js/app.js:152 (renderCommitHeader) and web/static/js/resize.js (MIN or MAX bounds).

Verify: run umpire in a repo with multi-line commit bodies. Confirm each 72-column source line renders as a single visual line, the pane width is consistent across commits, and dragging still resizes.
notes:
First attempt (CSS-first: #commit-header width:fit-content, .commit-message-body and textarea monospace at width:72ch, plus max-width:50vw) was implemented and verified in-browser, but Zach didn't like how it turned out, so it was dropped. The dropped commit was titled 'feat(commit pane): size the message pane to fit a 72-column body'. Reopening to explore a different direction. The problem statement in the description still stands, but disregard the CSS-first recommended approach.
The squash in umpire-6kw rewrote the SHA cited in the close reason: 94e5f52 is now 7a9db6c on main (the combined feat(commit pane) commit).
close_reason: Second approach, after the CSS/monospace one was dropped. sizeCommitHeader in web/static/js/app.js measures a fixed 72-char reference string in the body's own proportional font, pads it 10 percent, and sets #commit-header width, clamped to the Resize 200-800 bounds and capped at 50vw. Keeps white-space:pre-wrap so a dragged-narrow pane wraps instead of overflowing (the thing Zach disliked before). Drag-to-resize still overrides, and the diff pane flex:1 takes the leftover. Verified in-browser: 697px pane on a 1440 window, identical across commits, no double-wrap, no horizontal overflow, and confirmed it still wraps when narrowed to 320px. Committed in 94e5f52.
